capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 67.5 kWh nominal / 64.0 usable for the European 64 kWh Kona (same pack as North America 2019-2023; Weekly Driver gives 3P98S, 356 V). Hyundai NA marketed it as "64 kWh".

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 64.0 kWh usable (67.5 nominal) for the 64 kWh Kona Electric (MY20-21 page; MY22-23 page the same, src-evdb-kona-64-my22-23). Compared 2019-2023, same generation and pack. The Weekly Driver calls 64 kWh total: conflict.

chemistry.notes: NCM 622 cathode (LG Chem pouch cells) for the Kona Electric 2019-2023.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Electric Revs (Dec 2018, 2019 Kona Electric) says Canadian cars have a 2 kW battery heater and a driver-selected Winter Mode that warms the pack for quicker DC charging (the heater also runs on its own when very cold); no navigation trigger is described. US-market cars have no battery heater (Electric Revs, InsideEVs), so for US cars the real behaviour is closer to none; the field is shared by both markets, so the Canadian behaviour is recorded. EV Database lists preconditioning as not supported for the European MY22-23 car. No owner's manual page found.

dc_max_kw.notes: 77 kW peak (Weekly Driver; EV Database also 77 kW for MY20-23). Hyundai US marketed 100 kW DC fast charging (xautoworld relays, 0-80 % about 54 min at 100 kW), which is the charger rating, not the car's peak. Conflict noted.

ac_max_kw.notes: Hyundai US launch material: 7.2 kW Level II onboard charger (also Weekly Driver). European car is 11 kW three-phase; North America 7.2 kW.
